item: The Scout Fabric has no autonomous discovery (CRAWL): candidate sources are a fixed, committed catalogue file, never generated by observing world-model gaps or forecast error as the blueprint's Discovery Agent Loop specifies
why: `rg -n 'follow_links|expand_from|fn crawl\(' backend/crates/services/qip-data-finder/src` returns nothing, confirming the current-state record. `DiscoveryDesk` (discovery.rs) and `DataFinder::assess` implement everything downstream of a candidate list — probe, classify, assess legality, score, route, register — to a hardened, type-enforced standard, but every candidate still comes from `qip_data_finder::catalogue::load(text, now)` reading a file a human wrote at `main.rs:1059-1083`. The blueprint's step 1 ('observe gaps in the world model, strategies and forecast errors') and step 2 ('generate source-discovery queries... by geography, entity, domain and language') have no code path at all: nothing here reads `WorldModel`'s coverage or the falsification ledger to propose a new source. Migrating rather than rewriting is straightforward because the admission/legality/scoring gate the crawler would feed is already built and tested.

item: `qip_data_finder::ingestion::plan_for` / `descriptor_for` — the function that would turn a registered source into an operational ingestion plan — is called only from the crate's own lifecycle test, never from any composition root
why: `rg -n 'plan_for\(|descriptor_for\(' backend/crates` shows the two call sites are `ingestion.rs` itself (line 80, `descriptor_for` calling `plan_for`) and `tests/lifecycle.rs:184,195`; no non-test line in `crates/apps` or `crates/runtime` calls either. A `RegisteredSource` today goes admission → registration → nothing: `qip-api`/`qip-fastbrain` resolve a feed through `ConnectorFeed::open`/`shipped_class` instead, bypassing `IngestionPlan` entirely. Either this is the missing link the E08 adapter-lifecycle work is supposed to wire in, or it has been superseded by the shipped-manifest path and is stale scaffolding; the evidence needed is which the plan intends, not a code guess.
blueprint_refs: v11.6 §6.3 Pass-Through Acquisition and Knowledge Distillation (step 4: 'instantiate a feed/adapter in sandbox')

item: Two of the seven 'shipped, real' connectors (Kalshi, Alpaca) carry `LicensingPosture::Ambiguous` in the admission catalogue, so `admit()` structurally refuses them in production regardless of the connector code's own maturity
why: `catalogue()`'s `kalshi-markets` and `alpaca-daily-bars` entries (admission.rs:378-397) both hold `LicensingPosture::ambiguous("...terms... have not been read against this platform's usages; ADR 0034 names the source as a candidate only")`. `LicensingPosture::legality_for` maps `Ambiguous` to `Legality::unknown` (legal.rs:365-368), and this crate's own structural guarantee is that `admit` never proceeds on `Unknown`. So `KalshiMarketsConnector` and `AlpacaBarsConnector` — counted among qip-market-ingestion's 'seven real, shipped connectors' in its own purpose statement and covered by 62 connector-level tests — can never be admitted into a real run until a human reads each vendor's terms of service and either replaces the posture with `Declared` or confirms `Forbidden`. This is not fixable by writing more Rust; the evidence needed is the legal review ADR 0034 already flags as outstanding.

item: The four vendor adapters (rest/narrative/depth/alternative — ~2,500 lines, 210 tests) are complete and hardened but no vendor base_url/credential is configured for any of them anywhere in the repository
why: `rg -n production_requirement` on the four files confirms every `SourceDescriptor::production_requirement` is unconditionally `Some(self.requirement())` — there is no code path in which any of the four reports itself fit for production. `depth.rs` is the only one of the four holding live book state (rebuild-on-gap via qip-sequencing/qip-orderbook) and is the closest thing this build has to blueprint §8.1's L2/L3 depth requirement, and it has never processed a real message. The implementation and its 210 tests are real engineering, not a stub; what is missing is an operator supplying a vendor, which is a deployment/procurement action rather than a further code change.

item: No environment in this build has ever subscribed to a licensed live feed; default node startup always falls back to the synthetic generator
why: Confirmed against `main.rs:434-460`: with no `--tape`/`--replay` flag the node always constructs `SyntheticEnvironment::demo`. This is not a silent shortcut — every synthetic record is stamped `LicensingClass::Synthetic` and the type system refuses it as a production decision input — but it does mean that, today, zero of the platform's environments (dev included) ever ingest a real observation. Combined with finding 3 (2 of 7 admissible sources blocked on legal review) only five sources (coinbase, ecb, nyfed, nws, and whichever of kalshi/alpaca clears review) could ever be live, and none is configured. Evidence needed: a committed plan or date for standing up at least one real feed in a real environment, since 'strictly paper trading' is a boundary on order submission, not a reason to run permanently on synthetic data.
blueprint_refs: GCP v2.1 §2.1 World Data Pass-Through / Knowledge Persistence Invariant

item: Two independently-versioned, non-composing event envelopes exist in the sensed-data path, contradicting qip-streaming's own explicit 'one event history' invariant
why: qip-streaming's own module doc says: 'a second parallel envelope would be the worst possible outcome for a platform whose whole audit story is that there is one event history' and claims 'Everything the platform senses enters through here... wearing the same envelope' (lib.rs:1-17). `rg -n 'qip_streaming::' backend/crates/services/qip-market-ingestion/src backend/crates/services/qip-data-finder/src` returns nothing — the SENSE-stage crates never import qip-streaming at all. Every `SensedRecord` is instead wrapped in `MarketEventEnvelope` (connector/envelope.rs:86, its own `SchemaVersion`), and `StreamEnvelope::seal` (envelope.rs:181) is called only from `qip-kernel/src/platform.rs` (7 call sites, all for cycle/decision/order facts, not for connector output). The two schemas do not compose — neither wraps the other — which is precisely the 'second parallel envelope' the doc warns against, and it is already in production, not a hypothetical.
blueprint_refs: v11.6 §26.1 (wire format: 'never leak unversioned memory formats onto the network')

item: qip-kernel's stream journal has exactly one construction site and it is always the in-memory transport; the file-backed constructor the same type offers is never called
why: `rg -n 'DurableLogTransport::in_memory|journal:' backend/crates/runtime/qip-kernel/src/platform.rs` shows the private `journal` field (platform.rs:623) has one constructor call (platform.rs:4486) and it is always `::in_memory("kernel-journal")`; `DurableLogTransport::open` (durable.rs, file-backed) has zero callers in qip-kernel. Governance calls the event log 'hash-chained on purpose' and says 'nothing may write a record that cannot be replayed' — a journal that never survives a process restart cannot be replayed after one. This corroborates, from qip-streaming's own construction site, the same underlying fact `docs/reports/tech-debt/libs-foundation.json` raised for `QIP_STORAGE_TARGET=memory` at the central-plane storage layer; this entry is the equivalent gap in the stream-journal type itself, which offers a real alternative constructor nothing calls.

item: MeshTransport and PubSubTransport are complete, tested Publisher/Subscriber implementations that no composition root ever constructs
why: `rg -n 'MeshTransport::|PubSubTransport::' backend/crates/apps backend/crates/runtime --glob '!**/tests/**'` returns nothing; both are constructed only from qip-streaming's own `tests/`/`registry.rs` helper. Both are honestly documented as deliberately incomplete rather than as a shortcut — pubsub.rs states it 'never falls back' and 'never fakes a connection', and mesh.rs explains the ADR-0011/ADR-0009 dependency-direction reasoning for living where it does — so this is not a safety problem, it is scope not yet spent: no composition root can today reach a durable cross-process transport for anything routed `RoutingClass::Durable`.
blueprint_refs: v11.6 §26.1 fabric-bridge / Native Rust Event & Control Fabric

item: IngestionService — the Telemetry-wired SENSE-stage wrapper with three metric-recording sites — is never constructed by any deployed binary
why: `rg -n 'IngestionService::new|IngestionService::' backend/crates --glob '!**/tests/**'` returns only `service.rs` itself; `qip-api` and `qip-fastbrain` call `ConnectorFeed::open` directly instead of going through `IngestionService`. Its three `self.telemetry.metrics.count(...)`/`observe_latency_ms(...)` sites (service.rs:174,185,216) therefore never fire in a running process — the SENSE-stage-specific instance of the platform-wide 'nothing writes to Telemetry' gap `.claude/rules/domains/observability.md` already tracks at large.
blueprint_refs: v11.6 §8.2 Tick Data Pipeline and Storage

item: NetworkProbe — the one place qip-data-finder opens a real, credential-less socket in production — has zero dedicated unit tests
why: The current-state record's own `tests.count` for this module is 0, and it is exercised only indirectly through `tiers.rs`, `legality.rs` and `discovery.rs`'s own `DiscoveryDesk` test. `NetworkProbe::through` (probe.rs:418) is real network I/O reached directly from production (`discovery.rs:181`, one probe per candidate per assessment pass) and carries SSRF-relevant refusal logic (refuses `https://`, refuses an empty user agent) — exactly the class of code `.claude/rules/architecture/01-testing-strategy.md` wants directly proven, not only exercised as a side effect of a higher-level test that happens to construct one.
blueprint_refs: v11.6 §7 Evidence, Provenance & Truth Fabric (Authenticity mechanism)

item: qip-data-finder's module doc still describes NetworkProbe as an unimplemented stub; the real ADR-0060 client has shipped and the doc was never updated
why: Both locations describe `NetworkProbe` as reporting `Error::Unavailable` naming what production must supply, but the current implementation (probe.rs:403-528) is a real HTTP client that only returns `Unavailable` on a genuine failed request. A reader trusting the doc comment would believe probing is unimplemented when it has been live in production since ADR 0060 (discovery.rs:181). Already named in the current-state record's own gaps_observed; carried forward here because it is the kind of doc-vs-implementation drift this platform's governance rules have already been burned by elsewhere and it is a trivial, low-risk fix.

item: Causal-hypothesis provenance covers 1 of the blueprint's 6 named sources in production: only the platform's own DetectedAnomaly path ever proposes a causal edge
why: `HypothesisSource` (falsification.rs:90-106) has 7 variants: 6 named `BLUEPRINT_SOURCES: usize = 6` at falsification.rs:124 (CausalGraphGap, HighSurpriseEpisode, CounterfactualAnomaly, WorldModelTraversal, LanguageModelProposal, CrossAssetTransfer) plus the platform's own `DetectedAnomaly`. `rg -n 'SourceCensus|HypothesisSource::' backend/crates/runtime/qip-kernel/src --glob '!**/tests/**'` shows exactly one call — `census.record(HypothesisSource::DetectedAnomaly)` at `qip-kernel/src/falsification.rs:253` — and the surrounding comment is explicit that this is deliberate ('a second producer of hypotheses would have to record its own source here; until one exists, claiming any other source would put a number against a path that does not run'), which makes this a disclosed limitation rather than a hidden one. It still means the REASON stage's causal-discovery breadth is 1/6 of the blueprint's own table (cited in-code as '§14.2'), and GCP v2.1 §21.2 step 3 names surprise/novelty detection and causal-implication detection as two separate ambient triggers this build collapses into the single detector it has.

item: qip-chain — a complete, 69-test implementation of the blueprint's on-chain data requirement — is reached from production nowhere: observe_chain and every ChainAdapter are called only from tests
why: `rg -n observe_chain backend/crates` shows the single production definition (`platform.rs:16011`) and every call site under a `tests/` directory across three suites; `rg -n 'SyntheticChain::|JsonRpcChainAdapter::|NodeChainAdapter::' backend/crates/apps backend/crates/runtime --glob '!**/tests/**'` returns nothing, so no `ChainAdapter` is ever constructed outside qip-chain's own tests either. Blueprint §6.1 lists 'blockchain state, mempools, token flows, smart-contract events and protocol governance' as one of seven source-universe categories, and §9.1 names a dedicated 'Crypto/On-chain Brain' specialist. This crate is the only implementation of that brain anywhere in the tree — reorg-aware ChainState, a real JSON-RPC client (rpc.rs, 1188 lines), AMM/mempool/bridge modelling — and it is entirely dark in every deployed binary. Migration (wiring an existing, hardened crate into a composition root) applies cleanly here; nothing about the implementation itself needs to change.

item: Schema-drift detection is implemented and tested but never invoked in production, so its own tested guarantee ('a source that changes shape mid-stream is caught') does not hold in a deployed process
why: `SchemaSpec::drift_to` (schema.rs:164) is the only place a schema comparison happens — proven by the crate's own `schema_drift.rs` test named in the current-state record ('a source that changes shape mid-stream is caught, not silently absorbed') — but `rg -n 'drift_to\(|SchemaDrift::' backend/crates --glob '!**/tests/**'` finds zero callers outside qip-data-finder's own tests. `SourceQuality` (quality.rs:14, distinct from the sibling `SourceCost` at quality.rs:87 which *is* used in `discovery.rs`) is equally unreached. `SourceSchema` and `SourceCost` themselves do reach production via `discovery.rs`/`campaign.rs`/`references.rs`, but the drift-comparison and quality-scoring logic built on top of them do not — so a source that silently reshapes its payload in a real deployment is not, in fact, caught; only the test binary catches it.
blueprint_refs: GCP v2.1 §2.1 Source Manifest Registry (freshness / re-fetch instructions)

item: Only 7 real venues/vendors are shipped, with no listed-options, futures, or broad equities-exchange tape — well short of blueprint §8.1's tick-universe breadth
why: Confirmed by reading connectors/mod.rs: the shipped set is a crypto ticker (Coinbase), two FX/rate sources (Frankfurter, ECB), one US rate (NY Fed), a weather-station feed (NWS), a prediction market (Kalshi — itself blocked, see finding 3), and one equities-bars connector (Alpaca — also blocked). Blueprint §8.1 names trades/quotes/NBBO, L1/L2/L3 depth, options chains with implied-volatility surfaces and Greeks, and futures curves/basis/funding as first-class tick-universe members; none of those exists in this build. This is a scope/roadmap gap rather than a defect in what exists — the connector framework and contract-test harness both generalise cleanly — so the evidence needed is which additional venues are in scope next and under what licensing, which ties directly to findings 3 and 5.
